name: PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: CPIN — the quarter held the margin and the depreciation basis is now consistent
frontmatter.summary: The September quarter changes no operating assumption: sales and profit are the nine-month actuals already modelled. What did change is the accounting basis — the pack's depreciation is a cash-flow artefact, so EBITDA is rebuilt inside the company's own operating expense — and the earnings cross-checks now sit on the peer floor rather than an own-history mean that no longer describes the market. Target Rp3,945 on a total return of 70.4%.
thesis: The nine-month result remains an actual, not a forecast — sales of IDR60,200bn against IDR50,600bn and attributable profit of IDR5,180bn — and the chick-price circular changes no modelled line [S2, S11, S15].

Depreciation is the correction: the pack's IDR310bn against IDR18,060bn of property, plant and equipment is a cash-flow artefact, so EBITDA is rebuilt on the asset roll's own 2.4% bound with EBIT left on the company's operating expense [S0].

Working capital is the year's cash event: 28.5% of revenue at 30 September against IDR16,106bn at the year-end, funded with debt, so FY2026E free cash flow to the firm is IDR-335bn before the fourth quarter's collection [S0].

The cross-checks bracket the price rather than the DCF: the peer P/E of 5.3 times and EV/EBITDA of 4.9 times, applied to the last twelve months' earnings, give Rp2,398 and Rp2,665 against Rp2,450, so the return above the price is the cash flow the DCF capitalises, not a re-rating bet [S0].
The circular keeps the ceiling at the farm gate, adds a floor and drops the ex-factory reference; the direction is ambiguous and nothing is booked [S11, S2].

catalysts.event: First full quarter under the DOC final-stock guidance and the new price references
FY2026 audited statements — the depreciation note is the test this report cannot yet run
Annual general meeting and the FY2026 dividend declaration

blocks.text: Rating BUY, target Rp3,945, a total return of 70.4% from Rp2,450 [S0]. This note takes in the September quarter. The quarter is an actual, not an estimate — nine-month sales of IDR60,200bn and attributable profit of IDR5,180bn, with the September quarter the strongest of the three on sales [S2, S0]. The gross margin, tax rate and fourth-quarter growth rate were already the witnessed ones [S0, S2].

Two things changed, and neither is a change to the operating forecast. The first is the accounting basis of EBITDA. The pack's depreciation field is a direct-cash-flow artefact — it charges IDR310bn against IDR18,060bn of property, plant and equipment, a fifty-eight-year life — while the company's real charge sits inside the operating expense the pack derives by subtraction. The prior version restored that charge from a ten-year blended life, which put it above the asset roll the audited year supports; this version charges the roll's own bound, 2.4% of sales, so total operating expense stays the company's own 6.1%, EBIT is not moved by the choice, and EBITDA adds the charge back once [S0]. The second is the multiple level the cross-checks apply, not the earnings basis. Moving both onto the last twelve months — the same trailing period the peer medians are struck on — lifted the legs, but the multiples fall from an own-history mean to the peer median at 5.3 and 4.9 times: that choice, not the earnings, cuts the target by about a quarter to Rp3,945 while the DCF rises, and section four reconciles it leg by leg [S0, S2].

Working capital is what the quarter actually delivered. Inventory and receivables at 30 September took operating working capital to 28.5% of revenue against IDR16,106bn at the audited year-end, funded with borrowings, so FY2026E free cash flow to the firm is IDR-335bn before the December quarter [S0]. That is why the target sits where it does: the cross-checks land at and just above the price while the DCF sits well above it, so the return is the cash flow, not a re-rating [S0]. The 10 November 2026 Bapanas circular No. 456/2026 reset the references it monitors — a farm-gate chick band from Rp6,500 to Rp7,000, the ex-factory reference of Rp11,000 dropped, and a request to cut chick final stock by up to 17.0% [S11, S13]. The ceiling that binds a farmer is unchanged; the floor and the lost factory reference are new, and with no published pass-through elasticity the direction is stated and nothing is booked [S2, S11, S12, S13].

CPIN is Indonesia's largest poultry and animal-feed group, integrated from feed mill to plate. Nine-month segment sales were IDR26,980bn from broiler growing, IDR20,740bn from feed, IDR8,150bn from processed chicken, IDR3,440bn from day-old chicks and IDR892bn from other activities, with chicks at IDR3,500bn of a IDR70,700bn top line last year [S2, S5]. Because it sells the feed, the chick and the bird, a lower feed cost reaches it twice [S2].

Sales are domestic: IDR59,940bn inside Indonesia against IDR256bn of exports [S2], so currency and the global feed complex arrive through costs, not demand [S2, S0]. Control sits in Thailand: the Jiaravanon family holds 55.5% through Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Group, with the remaining register covered under governance [S5].

The chick business is the smallest named segment at IDR3,440bn of nine-month sales, and the statements do not split it between third-party farmers and the group's own houses, so we assert no split we cannot source [S2]. Strategy is capacity and integration: in August 2025 it bought breeding facilities from PT Satwa Utama Raya for IDR431bn, a ninety-nine per cent-controlled affiliate, so the deal is related-party [S6].

The economics are set by two prices the company does not control: feed grain and the live bird. The nine-month result shows what happens when the first falls faster than the second — sales of IDR60,200bn against cost of goods sold of IDR49,600bn and profit before tax of IDR6,680bn [S2]. With feed a third of sales, a feed-cost move is felt on both sides [S2].

Policy has been reset around reference prices. The circular fixes the broiler chick band at Rp6,500 to Rp7,000, a producer reference for chicken meat of Rp25,000, a retail ceiling for dry corn of Rp5,800 and consumer ceilings for eggs and sugar [S11]. For an integrated producer it is two-sided: it caps what the chick business can charge while setting references further up the chain that would support the meat price [S11].

The grain side has its own interventions: 242 kt of SPHP feed corn for small layer farmers from March 2026 [S8], small against a leader selling IDR20,740bn of feed in nine months, and a November warehouse-receipt scheme linking corn farmers and cooperatives [S9]. Both are reversible.

The cycle is visible in the trade press: live-bird prices fell to Rp22,000 in October against a farmer cost of production above that level [S13, S12]. Hence the request for a chick-supply cut: the industry oversupplied chicks and pushed the bird price below cost, so the margin is a level to hold, not to extrapolate [S12, S13].

Demand has a policy leg but no usable number: the free nutritious meals programme puts chicken and eggs into institutional menus, but the only volumes in the sources belong to competitors and none gives CPIN's scale, so no institutional volume is carried [S3]. The moat is distribution density and integration, which protects the cost position, not the selling price: supplier power is high in corn and soymeal, buyer power moderate, entry barred by capital and biosecurity, rivalry intense and cyclical [S3, S8].

History. The last four audited years show steady top-line growth and profit that moves in a cycle: revenue rose from IDR56,868bn to IDR70,705bn, with operating profit falling in the middle before recovering to IDR8,133bn [S0].

Forecast. FY2026E revenue of IDR84,139bn carries the nine-month actual and runs the fourth quarter at the witnessed rate; growth then steps down to 7.0% and tapers to the macro deck's long-run rate, because sales are almost entirely domestic and no source discloses capacity that would repeat this year [S0, S2]. The circular enters no line: we have no sourced volume or price change for it [S2, S11].

The EBITDA bridge. EBIT of IDR9,758bn stays on the company's own basis — gross profit of IDR14,861bn less operating expense of IDR5,103bn — and that expense already contains depreciation, being what is left of gross profit after reported EBIT [S0]. EBITDA of IDR11,813bn at a 14.0% margin adds the charge back once, at IDR2,055bn. That charge is a derivation: the pack's line is IDR310bn, a fifty-eight-year life against IDR18,060bn of assets, while the real charge sits inside the operating expense. The audited asset roll bounds it from above — opening, capex, the IDR431bn affiliate purchase and closing balances leave a maximum — and the model charges that bound, not a blended-life estimate above it [S0, S6]; the IDR2,187bn of non-cash add-backs in the pack's cash flow is not a depreciation measure and is not used. On the restated charge the audited year's EBITDA margin is within a tenth of the forecast's, so the step from 11.9% is the basis change, not an operating improvement, and the audited columns keep the pack's charge, which is why the printed line jumps [S0].

Actual against forecast. The nine months landed where the model carried them: sales of IDR60,200bn and attributable profit of IDR5,180bn are already most of the IDR84,139bn and IDR7,224bn forecast for the year, so the run rate is set by the margin rather than volume, which is what the model holds through the fourth quarter [S2, S0].

Margins. The witnessed rate is the anchor and it is held: realised gross margin is 17.7% in FY2026E, 17.7% in FY2027E and 17.3% in FY2028E [S0, S2]. The input behind it, 20.0%, is a calibrated residual: the engine charges the deck's corn and soymeal curves on top, so the input is the margin at the FY2025A input cost rather than a rate any year earned on its reported basis, and the two together reproduce the witnessed margin [S0]. Corn is carried at 19.0% of cost of goods sold and soymeal at 9.0%, ordered from the segment mix rather than published input bills [S2, S8]. Overhead is the company's own 6.1% of sales, of which 2.4% is depreciation [S0]. Tax is set to 22.5%, the rate implied by nine-month profit before tax of IDR6,680bn against attributable profit of IDR5,180bn [S2].

Cash flow, capex and working capital. Operating working capital runs at 28.5% of revenue against IDR16,106bn at the audited year-end, absorbing IDR7,849bn in FY2026E against IDR2,103bn of capex — the main constraint on distributable cash [S0]. That build is the witnessed nine months plus the December quarter at the same intensity, carried rather than reverted, because a return to the three-year average is an assumption the September balance sheet contradicts [S0]. Free cash flow to the firm is therefore IDR-335bn in FY2026E, negative on the stub, and IDR6,363bn in FY2027E once the ratio is flat [S0]. Capex is held at the last audited 2.5% of sales; the breeding purchase of IDR431bn sits in investing cash flow [S0, S6].

Balance sheet, valuation date and dividend. The valuation date is 30 September 2026, the pack's latest balance sheet: FY2026E cash flow is counted only from 1 October and the bridge deducts that date's net debt, not the December year-end figure the forecast roll produces [S0]. Gross borrowings of IDR11,595bn are carried at their September level, and the September cash balance is lower than the IDR5,769bn the year-end roll shows, so the deduction the target uses is larger than the IDR5,826bn of net debt printed for the December year: the December quarter is the group's strongest cash quarter and its collection has not happened at the valuation date [S0]. Net debt at the audited year-end was IDR2,201bn, or 0.3 times EBITDA. Nine-month interest annualises to the IDR524bn charged at 7.9%, the marginal quarter within a tenth of a point of it [S0]. Equity of IDR36,380bn and total assets of IDR53,260bn corroborate the size of the balance sheet [S0, S2]. Return on equity was 17.5%, forecast at 19.9% [S2, S0]. For 2025 the board declared Rp180 a share, IDR2,950bn in total, 52.3% of profit, held flat [S5, S7].

Earnings-quality flags. Run on the nine-month data, the house screen gives one flag, the working-capital one: last-twelve-month operating cash flow is a small fraction of last-twelve-month profit, so the accruals ratio clears the ten per cent screen on a build of IDR7,849bn [S0]. Through the direct-method convention that also produces the pack's depreciation line we classify it optics-class: it is disclosed, it is inventory and farmer credit rather than aged receivables, the audited year converted at roughly one times profit, and the December quarter is the collection quarter [S0]. It is why the bear carries a working-capital leg, and a second year of it at the FY2026 audit would stop being optics [S0]. Receivables grew faster than revenue and inventory faster than cost of goods sold [S0]. The profit improvement is a margin effect, the higher-quality kind, but policy-dependent and reversible [S2, S8].

Why this method set. A DCF is primary with earnings and EBITDA multiples as cross-checks, because value comes from the cash a going concern converts over a cycle rather than from a finite reserve [S0]. The compounder card's discipline applies: growth is paid for by reinvestment, the discount rate is inside the house band, and the terminal value goes through the multiple-survival test [S0]. Growth is paid for and fades: capex plus the working-capital build absorbs roughly half of after-tax operating profit by FY2035E, and return on equity falls from 19.9% to 13.1% against a 13.2% cost of equity — that convergence is the fade year, and the reason terminal growth is 4.0% [S0].

The cost of capital. The house build runs a rupiah risk-free rate of 7.4%, deducts the default spread of 1.6% and adds the levered beta of 1.10 — an unlevered 0.90 levered at a debt-to-equity of 0.29 — times the mature premium of 4.2% plus the country premium of 2.5%: a cost of equity of 13.2% and, with pre-tax debt at 9.4% and a gross-debt weight of 22.4%, a WACC of 11.9%, inside the house band [S0]. The debt weight is gross borrowings at 30 September over market equity, not net debt: on net debt it would be roughly half and the WACC some two-fifths of a point lower, and the gross figure is used because the DCF discounts enterprise cash flow against the debt that exists [S0]. That pre-tax debt cost of 9.4% is the house build, above the 7.9% the finance line actually pays — whose marginal quarter is within a tenth of a point of it — so the cheaper DCF leg is discounted about a quarter point of WACC too hard; the direction is conservative and disclosed rather than aligned [S0]. The cost of equity lands a fifth of a point above the band; that overshoot is disclosed, not massaged through the beta, and it affects the twelve-month roll rather than the DCF [S0].

The primary method. The DCF values the equity at Rp4,505, above the Rp2,450 price, terminal value at 49.1% of the total — the right shape when near-term cash conversion is the question [S0]. Operating working capital is the drag: at 28.5% of revenue and with sales growing, inventory and receivables rival capex every year, and the stub year is negative at IDR-335bn [S0].

The cross-checks and the divergence. The P/E check gives Rp2,398 on 5.3 times the last twelve months' attributable profit and the EV/EBITDA check Rp2,665 on 4.9 times last-twelve-month EBITDA — the trailing period the peer medians are trailing multiples of, not the last audited year, whose earnings the recovery had left behind [S0, S2]. On that basis the legs are -46.8% and -40.8% against the primary and bracket the price rather than sit far below it: the multiple legs ask what the sector pays today for the earnings actually delivered, the DCF what the cash flow is worth if the margin holds, so the gap is a basis gap as much as a multiple gap [S0]. The peer set is narrower than a summary line suggests: CPIN's FY2025A multiple of 7.1x times sits above the median of 5.3 times and below two higher prints, but that is the audited year — on the last-twelve-month basis the legs use, the shares trade at that median, not above it, because the recovery is in the denominator [S0, S2]. The median is the mean of two middle observations out of six, and one observation is a near-zero print from a dormant shell that is not a multiple at all; on EBITDA, the same 5.0x FY2025A figure against a median of 4.9 times on a set of five [S0]. The legs use the peer median, not CPIN's own history — four annual observations spanning a re-rating and a de-rating, whose mean is computed from the price it is then used to value [S0]. The target is therefore not the DCF: Rp3,505 rolled at the cost of equity net of the Rp230 dividend is Rp3,737, and the 50.0% base at Rp3,737, the 25.0% bear at Rp2,186 and the 25.0% bull at Rp6,121 give the Rp3,945 target, dated twelve months from the 30 September anchor [S0].

The target move reconciled. The prior published target was five thousand two hundred and forty rupiah a share on 12 November, struck on own-history mean multiples — about fourteen and seven-tenths times earnings, ten and four-tenths times EBITDA — with the same leg weights and an earlier DCF of four thousand three hundred and eighty-two rupiah. The DCF, now on the bound depreciation charge, is Rp4,505; the multiples are the peer medians, so the legs are Rp2,398 and Rp2,665, roughly half of what each was worth; the blend is Rp3,505, the twelve-month roll Rp3,737 and the scenario weighting Rp3,945. The earnings-basis move raised the legs; the multiple level, own-history mean to peer median, is the whole of the quarter cut, and the DCF sits higher [S0].

The multiple the call needs. Both earnings legs apply the peer median — 5.3 times last-twelve-month earnings against CPIN's FY2025A 7.1x, and 4.9 against 5.0x — and on that trailing basis the shares already trade there [S0]. They land at Rp2,398 and Rp2,665 against a Rp2,450 price, so the shares are worth about what they cost and the return above the price is the cash flow the DCF capitalises. The judgment the call rests on is narrow — that the market's lowest peer multiple is the wrong permanent level for a business earning the 19.9% return the model shows [S0, S2].

The terminal test and the implied price. The compounder card's multiple-survival test is run on the model's undiscounted terminal value against the terminal year's EBITDA and EBIT, and it fails plainly: the terminal block capitalises FY2035E EBITDA of IDR16,292bn and EBIT of IDR13,028bn at an exit multiple above the 5.0x the shares trade on and far above the 3.9x the price pays for FY2026E EBITDA, so the implied exit is a re-rating from the entry [S0]. That is multiple expansion wearing a DCF costume, and it is what a 4.0% perpetuity at a 11.9% discount rate arithmetically implies: the terminal value is 49.1% of enterprise value and its growth is assumed, not earned by reinvestment. A terminal EBITDA margin of 12.2%, below FY2026E, is not peak economics, but the exit multiple is the card's own fail condition — which is why half the target weight is written down to the peer median instead [S0]. The price is the mirror image: at Rp2,450 the market capitalises FY2026E earnings at 5.6x and enterprise value at 3.9x of EBITDA, priced for a trough on both counts, and the reverse DCF cannot bracket the price, so the reading is stated: the market does not believe the margin lasts, not that the cash is missing [S0].

The first table moves the discount rate against terminal growth, the second revenue growth against gross margin, and the gross-margin rows move the target far more, so a different answer should come from the margin [S0]. The depreciation split carries a one-sided bound rather than a grid: the charge is the asset roll's own maximum, so the error can only be that the true charge is lower, which lifts EBITDA and the DCF; holding the pack's own line instead would move value by less than the smallest discount-rate step, and the other direction is excluded by the roll [S0, S6].

The scenario set is a pure operating mirror, and it can fail. The bear reproduces the weakest quarter the company printed this year — the second, whose realised gross margin sits well below the nine-month average — and holds it: corn above the deck's forward curve the base already charges from FY2026E while broiler and chick prices set daily do not follow it up, and soymeal imported at a weaker rupiah [S0, S2, F3, F6]. Growth is slower, working-capital intensity higher and the cost of debt higher, each by the same step as the bull's opposite [S0]. The bull mirrors each of the four one for one, holding the best quarter's margin and reversing the working-capital build [S0]. The values are not mirrored even though the shocks are, because overhead, capex and working capital do not scale with the margin: a point of margin lost costs more than a point gained adds, so the bear at Rp2,186 is well below the Rp2,450 price while the bull at Rp6,121 is well above it [S0]. Named and not modelled: price realisation, with bird and chick prices set daily in a spot market the group does not clear [S3]; currency through imported soymeal; and biological risk, unquantified [S0]. The SPHP programme is too small to offset any of it [S8, F31].

That de-rating risk sits inside the base rather than as a fifth shock: the base multiple is already the peer median, 5.3 times, and on the trailing basis the shares trade there, so no further de-rating to the sector's current level is left to take — a sector-multiple valuation of the earnings delivered gives Rp2,398 on the P/E leg, about two-thirds of the base, and Rp2,665 on EBITDA — and a multiple shock on top would double-count it [S0].

The free nutritious meals programme and the chick documents are named and not scored. The pool has a policy leg, but the only volumes in the sources belong to competitors and CPIN discloses none, so no institutional volume is carried in the base or the bull [S3]. The new chick band's ceiling is the figure that bound the farmer before, the floor is new and the ex-factory reference is gone, and the circular does not say which binds [S11]; a cut of up to 17.0% in placements costs the chick segment, IDR3,440bn of nine-month revenue, and benefits broiler growing and processed chicken at IDR26,980bn and IDR8,150bn together — a book several times the size of the one it costs, an asymmetry a reader can size rather than a number in the model [S2, S13]. An enforced corn ceiling would cut the other way, hurting the farmers who supply the mill, so we expect it applied to traders rather than the mill's cost [S11, S12].

Liquidity is not the constraint: free float of 15.4% on a IDR40,175.1bn market value and IDR94.7bn of three-month turnover are adequate, and no liquidity discount is charged [S0]. Probabilities are 50.0% base at Rp3,737, 25.0% bear at Rp2,186 and 25.0% bull at Rp6,121 [S0]. The bear is below the price, so the call can fail on the company's own witnessed worst quarter: what would hurt the holder is another year of the working-capital build with the margin at the second quarter's level [S0].

Signposts. For the better: corn staying near the spot level rather than the forward curve; a second quarter of margin at the witnessed level with the nine-month working-capital build converting in the fourth quarter; evidence that the meat and corn references are enforced in the group's favour; the free-meals programme converting into contracted volume [S0, S11, S3]. For the worse: corn above the deck's curve with bird prices flat; working capital outrunning sales for a second year, which would take the accruals flag from optics-class to a real one; the chick band binding on realised prices or the supply guidance cutting placements by more than price recovers; a related-party transaction larger than the breeding purchase [S0, S11, S13, S6].

Ownership and control. The Jiaravanon family controls the company through Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Group at 55.5%, with public investors at 38.5% and UBS AG Singapore at 6.0% [S5]. The pack's register — free float 15.4%, insiders 71.5% [S0] — does not agree, and its lower float is used for the liquidity test [S0, S5]. The IDX screen finds no special-monitoring board status, no special-notation letter and no auditor change; the absence of a search result is not a clean bill and is recorded as a gap, and governance stays "not assessed" while the related-party flow table and the auditor are missing [S5, S6].

Related parties. The transaction we can source is the August 2025 breeding purchase from PT Satwa Utama Raya for IDR431bn, a ninety-nine per cent-controlled affiliate — an internal reorganisation disclosed to the exchange [S6]. No full related-party flow table is sourced, so that pre-thesis gate stays open and we do not assert the flows are small [S6].

Dividend record, board and ESG. The company pays a substantial and rising dividend: Rp180 a share for 2025, IDR2,950bn in total, 52.3% of profit [S5, S7]; a controller taking cash through dividends rather than related-party balances is the better version of concentrated ownership [S7]. Auditor identity and opinion could not be sourced, a gap reported as one [S6]. ESG exposures are biosecurity, animal welfare, antibiotic use in feed and labour intensity in processing, and the free-meals programme makes the product part of public nutrition policy, a reputational as well as demand exposure [S3].

The dated catalysts are the first full quarter under the supply guidance and the new references, the FY2026 audited statements and the FY2026 dividend [S13, S0, S7]. We watch four things: the gross margin, because it is the thesis and depends on corn [S2, S0]; the corn price and SPHP volume [S8, S9]; the working-capital ratio, which separates profit from distributable cash [S0]; and the gap between the chick band and CPIN's realised price, with the live-bird price [S11, S13].

bear.narrative: The quarter the company actually printed in 2026Q2 is the bear's anchor: gross profit of IDR2,490bn on revenue of IDR19,466bn is a 12.8 per cent gross margin, some 4.8 points below the nine-month realised rate (S0). The bear reproduces it rather than inventing a worse one, and holds it for the forecast: corn above the deck's forward curve, which the base already charges from FY2026E, while broiler and DOC prices set daily in the market do not follow it up (S0, S2, F3, F6); soymeal imported and the rupiah weaker, so the protein input costs more in rupiah at the same dollar price (S0). Growth is three points slower because the recovery year is not repeated. Working capital, the downside the quarter actually delivered, goes to 31.5 per cent of revenue, three points above the 28.5 per cent the September balance sheet already records, and the cost of debt rises a point on the witnessed IDR11,595bn of gross borrowings, taking the finance line toward the 8 per cent the marginal quarter already pays (S0). Four shocks, each mirrored one for one in the bull; no fifth unnamed haircut and no multiple shock, because the base multiple is already the market's trough peer median.

bull.narrative: The margin holds at the best quarter the company printed this year: 2026Q1 gross profit of IDR4,459bn on revenue of IDR19,952bn is a 22.3 per cent margin, 4.8 points above the nine-month realised rate, and the bull carries that level for the forecast (S0). Corn stays near the spot level rather than the higher forward path the base charges, so the witnessed margin is held rather than given back (S0). Growth is three points faster, working capital frees three points as the inventory built in the first nine months converts and farmer credit turns, and the cost of debt falls a point. The three policy legs are named but NOT in the numbers: the chick band's withdrawal of the ex-factory reference is producer-positive in direction (S11), the final-stock cut of 10-17 per cent lifts the broiler price into segments ten times the chick segment it costs (S13, S2), and the free-meals programme is a one-way omitted upside - S3 documents AYAM supplying about fifty kitchens and JPFA supplying cooperatives, and discloses no CPIN volume, so no institutional volume is carried here or in the base. The four shocks mirror the bear exactly, so the bull is the operating mirror of the bear plus three identified, unquantified upside legs a reader can size.

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the nine-month actual, not on a forecast: nine-month 2026 net sales were IDR 60,200bn against IDR 50,600bn a year earlier, +19.0 per cent (S2, F1, F2). FY2025's fourth quarter contributed the difference between the audited year and its own nine-month base; running that quarter at the witnessed growth rate gives the FY2026E rate carried here. Growth then steps down to the volume the domestic market can absorb: the group has already taken the recovery year (nine-month segment sales of broiler IDR 26,980bn, feed IDR 20,740bn, processed chicken IDR 8,150bn, DOC IDR 3,440bn, S2, F3-F6) and no source discloses new capacity that would repeat a twenty per cent year. The taper is to the house macro deck's long-run expansion for Indonesia plus population, not a haircut (S0).

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs (calibrated residual, pre-cost-link)
assumptions.basis: A calibrated residual, and labelled as one: the engine charges the deck's corn and soymeal curves through the two cost links on top of this input, so the number here is the margin at the FY2025A input cost, not a margin any year earned on its reported basis. FY2025A realised 17.6 per cent (S0) and the nine months of 2026 also realised 17.6 per cent: net sales of IDR60,200bn less cost of goods sold of IDR49,600bn (S2, F1, F10), against 16.0 per cent in the same nine months of 2025 (IDR50,600bn less IDR42,500bn, S2, F2, F10). The input carried here is the number that reproduces that witnessed realised margin after the links: the deck's corn and soymeal at their FY2026E values against their FY2025A base take about 2.3 points off the input, which is why 19.95 per cent produces a realised margin of about 17.6 per cent. Cost of goods sold grew slower than sales in the nine months, 16.7 against 19.0 per cent (S2, F1, F2, F10), so the margin is at its own recent level, not stretched. Because the cost links are charged separately, a one-point move in this input is a one-point move in the realised margin: the sensitivity table in section 4 is read in realised terms, not as a move off a reported year. The national SPHP feed-corn programme is a small, dated, reversible support for layer smallholders, 242kt against a feed business selling IDR20,740bn in nine months (S8, F31, S2, F4), not the reason a feed-to-plate group's margin is where it is. The deck's corn curve is charged from FY2026E (214.57 against a FY2025A base of 172.56, S0), not from FY2027E, so there is no step in the cost drivers between the two years and no give-back in the base case. A margin fall needs a sourced reason; none exists, so the caution sits in the bear scenario.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1 (corn): share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: An ordered estimate from the disclosed segments, because the company does not publish an input bill. Feed is IDR 20,740bn of IDR 60,200bn of nine-month sales, a third of the top line (S2, F4, F1); on a feed business that is mostly pass-through of raw material, feed is roughly a third of consolidated cost of goods sold. Corn is the industry's most important feed component (S8) and is conventionally rather more than half of a poultry feed formula, which puts corn at roughly one-fifth of group COGS. We carry that as an estimate and say so: the red team should read it as an ordered magnitude, not a disclosed number.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1 (corn): pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Sixty per cent. Feed mills re-price bagged feed to farmers with a lag and broiler and DOC prices are set daily in a spot market the group does not clear, so a corn move reaches the P&L in part and over time rather than in full. The witnessed year supports a high pass-through rather than a squeeze: a 17 per cent rise in cost of goods sold on a 19 per cent rise in sales left the margin wider, not narrower (S2, F1, F2, F10).

assumptions.label: Cost link 2 (soymeal): share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: The same ordered estimate for the second input: soymeal is the protein component of the feed formula and, on the feed share of consolidated COGS set out in the corn line above (S2, F4), lands near one-tenth of group cost of goods sold. Soymeal is imported and priced in dollars, so this link also carries the rupiah. Disclosed as an estimate, not a sourced figure.

assumptions.label: Cost link 2 (soymeal): pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Sixty per cent, mirroring the corn link: the same feed-price lag and the same spot protein market sit behind both, and no source supports treating the two inputs differently. Mirroring keeps the two cost channels from smuggling an unstated margin assumption into the base case.

assumptions.label: Operating expense incl. re‑split depreciation / revenue (the pack's total)
assumptions.basis: The pack's total, re-split rather than re-based. Operating expense is what is left of gross profit after EBIT - revenue less cost of goods sold less reported EBIT - so it already contains the depreciation the company charged, whatever the pack's separate D&A field says (S0). Holding the total at 6.07 per cent of sales keeps forecast EBIT on the basis the company reports and makes the depreciation question a re-split of one line instead of an extra charge: cash overhead is 3.62 per cent and depreciation 2.44 per cent, which sums to 6.07 per cent. The previous version carried 7.15 per cent, adding the restated depreciation to a cash ratio that had already had the pack's charge taken out of it, so it charged depreciation twice and understated EBIT by about 1.1 points of revenue; this corrects that and section 3 prints the EBITDA bridge from the pack's basis to this one. Cash overheads stay at the last audited year's real level, and nothing is re-based for the recovery.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue (re‑split out of total operating expense)
assumptions.basis: Re-split out of the pack's total, not added on top of it. The pack's own D&A field is the direct-cash-flow artefact: IDR310.5bn against IDR18,060bn of property, plant and equipment is a fifty-eight-year life (S0). The company's depreciation is nonetheless inside its reported EBIT, so the question is how much of the pack's IDR4,287.3bn operating-expense line it is. The FY2025A asset roll bounds it from above: opening IDR17,585bn plus capex IDR1,771bn plus the IDR430.98bn affiliate acquisition less the closing IDR18,060bn leaves IDR1,727bn for depreciation and disposals, so no depreciation charge carried this year can exceed the bound unless a revaluation or FX uplift is named, and none is disclosed (S0, S6, F30). We therefore charge the bound itself, IDR1,727bn, 2.44 per cent of FY2025A revenue, which leaves cash overheads at 3.62 per cent of the pack's 6.07 per cent total. The prior version's IDR1,800bn (2.55 per cent) sat above the roll and is withdrawn: it was inferred from a ten-year blended life that the roll does not support. The pack's IDR2,187bn of non-cash add-backs is a cash-flow total, not a depreciation measure, and is not used. This is a derivation from the pack, not a figure read off the depreciation note: the annual report and the LK are not in the source archive, so the two audited years keep the pack's line and cannot be restated as facts, and section 3 prints the EBITDA bridge from the pack's basis to this one. The FY2026 audited note is the test; charging the roll's own bound means the error can only be that the true charge is lower, which lifts EBITDA and the DCF. Because the charge sits inside a.opex_pct, EBIT is after depreciation and the add-back happens once.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own capital spending over revenue, held flat (S0). That is the only witnessed ratio: the group bought breeding facilities from an affiliated company for IDR 430.98bn in August 2025 (S6, F30), an acquisition that sits in investing cash flow rather than in the capex line, and we do not gross it up into the forecast.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The witnessed 30 September 2026 balance sheet, not the three-year average: non-cash current assets less non-debt current liabilities were IDR22,860.7bn on last-twelve-month revenue of IDR80,304.1bn, which is 28.47 per cent (S0). The pack's own line is built that way - at FY2025A it reproduces IDR16,105.5bn, or 22.8 per cent of that year's revenue - so the two dates are on one definition. The step up is real and is the year's central cash fact: inventory rose by IDR6,502bn in the nine months and payables fell, taking the nine-month build to IDR6,755bn. The company now runs at the higher intensity, so the forecast carries it every year; assuming a reversion to the three-year 21.1 per cent would be an unsourced assumption that the September balance sheet contradicts. Q4 is a high-revenue quarter, so the ratio at 31 December may print lower than 28.5 per cent; the forecast year-end stock and the witnessed Q3 stock are printed in section 3 so the reader can see that.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The witnessed nine-month rate, not the three-year engine default: profit before tax of IDR 6,680bn against profit attributable to the owners of IDR 5,180bn implies a charge near 22.5 per cent, and the minority interest is nil in the model (S2, F11, F12). That is the rate the business is paying now, it agrees with the 22 per cent statutory rate the discount-rate build uses, and holding the FY2023A-FY2025A average instead would charge the forecast at a rate the last actual does not show (S0).

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The witnessed 2026 rate, not the three-year average: nine-month interest expense of IDR392.6bn (quarterly charges of 90.1, 106.4 and 196.1, S0) annualises to IDR523.5bn, which is 7.86 per cent of the IDR6,662bn opening debt the engine charges it against; the marginal third quarter, IDR196.1bn on June-end debt of IDR9,849bn, is 7.97 per cent, so the two readings agree. The three-year default of 6.59 per cent is what the company paid before the 2026 borrowing and would understate the cost of the debt actually on the balance sheet.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The witnessed nine-month increase, not the engine default of zero: gross borrowings rose from IDR6,662bn at 31 December 2025 to IDR11,595bn at 30 September 2026, so IDR4,933bn is already drawn and belongs in the FY2026E balance sheet (S0). After FY2026E the forecast draws nothing more, because no source discloses a funding plan and a repayment would be as unsourced as a new drawdown; the debt stays at the September level and the interest line is charged on it. The engine's cash roll then reconciles to the witnessed date: with the corrected EBITDA, the September working-capital intensity and this drawdown, FY2026E year-end net debt lands within a few hundred billion of the IDR6,719bn the 30 September balance sheet records, where the previous version projected IDR294bn.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The declared ratio, not an assumption: the 2025 financial year was paid at a payout of 52.3 per cent of attributable profit (S5, F22), announced as 52.29 per cent with the IDR 180 per share distribution approved on 20 May 2026 (S7, F26, F27). The prior year was 47.7 per cent (S5), so the payout has stepped up rather than drifted, and we hold the current rate flat.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at 4.0 per cent, the rate every covered POULTRY_FEED peer (JPFA, MAIN, NEST, RLCO) uses on the same house macro deck, so the perpetuity is consistent across the industry rather than name-specific. It sits above the deck's 3.28 per cent CPI because it carries a little real volume: a protein business whose sales are nine-tenths domestic (S2, F8) grows with population and per-capita income, and its own revenue grew 4.8 per cent in a bad year (S5, F17). It remains below the deck's 5.29 per cent real GDP, so it does not assume share gain in perpetuity (S0).

challenges.challenge: The D&A restatement appears to double-count against opex. The pack has GP 12,420.5 less opex 4,287.3 equals EBIT 8,133.1 and EBITDA 8,443.6 equals EBIT plus D&A 310.5, so D&A sits inside opex. The forecast applies opex at the pack's 6.06% of revenue and then adds a separately restated D&A of 1,287, which leaves implied cash overheads of 4.53% of revenue against 5.63% in FY2025A. FY2026E EBITDA is therefore about 900 too high (11,049 against roughly 10,155) and most of the 13.1% margin step is the artefact, not an operating improvement.
challenges.answer: The double count is real and is removed. The pack opex is derived by subtraction (gross profit less reported EBIT), so depreciation already sits inside the 6.07 per cent of sales; the previous version added a restated charge on top of a ratio that had already had the pack charge taken out, understating EBIT by about 1.1 points of revenue. Opex is now held at the company own total with 2.55 per cent re-split out as D&A, so EBIT is untouched by the depreciation choice and EBITDA adds the charge back once. The calibration gap closed to two-tenths of a point: restated FY2025A EBITDA margin 14.05 per cent against 14.15 per cent forecast, so the step from the pack 11.9 per cent is the basis change, not an operating improvement. Section 3 prints the bridge and the three pack-internal anchors behind the charge [S0, S6].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 says "Accruals are clean" citing FY2025 (OCF 5,774 against NP 5,644), which is true of that year but not of the period this note reports. The same pack shows LTM OCF of 1,873 against LTM NP of 7,461, an accruals ratio of 11.3% on average assets of 49,564 (above the method card's 10% screen), NWC of 22,861 or 28.5% of LTM revenue against 22.8% at FY2025, and a nine-month NWC build of 6,756. That is the divergence flag the house card exists to catch, and the note converts it into a quality endorsement.
challenges.answer: Accruals are clean is gone from section 3 and section 6. The house screen is run on the nine-month data and returns one flag: last-twelve-month operating cash flow is a small fraction of last-twelve-month profit, so the accruals ratio is above the ten per cent screen on a working-capital build of the size the September balance sheet shows. It is classified optics-class, not manipulation-class, with four reasons in the report: disclosed, inventory and farmer credit rather than receivables aged past terms, the audited year converting at roughly one times profit, and the December quarter being the collection quarter. The direct-method convention behind the pack depreciation line is named as the reason we do not infer cleanliness from the pack, and the flag is why the bear carries a working-capital leg [S0, S2].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E FCFF of 5,131 implies operating cash flow near 6,900 (NP 7,293 plus D&A 1,287 less delta NWC 1,618) against the pack's LTM OCF of 1,873, and delta NWC of 1,618 against +6,756 in the nine months, with nwc_pct fixed at 21.07% against the 28.5% the 30 September balance sheet records. The DCF counts only the Q4 stub of FY2026E, so the near-term error is contained, but every subsequent year is discounted off a working-capital ratio the company no longer runs.
challenges.answer: nwc_pct is restated to the 30 September actual at 28.47 per cent of revenue and carried, not reverted, because a return to the three-year average is an assumption the September balance sheet contradicts. FY2026E absorbs the witnessed nine-month build plus the December quarter at the same intensity, so the delta is the witnessed step rather than the smaller figure challenged; free cash flow to the firm is negative on the stub and turns only once the ratio is flat. The DCF was rerun and the drag is stated in the primary-method paragraph: incremental inventory and receivables rival capex every year at this growth [S0].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E does not reproduce the last actual's financing. The model holds debt at 6,662 from FY2025A and charges interest of 439, but 30 September debt is 11,595 and nine-month interest is already 392. Net debt is projected at 294 for FY2026E and net cash of 1,629 for FY2027E, while the actual is 6,719 and rising; the Q4 stub alone (about 1,300 of FCFF) cannot clear 6,719 to 294.
challenges.answer: Debt is re-anchored to the 30 September balance sheet: gross borrowings of 11,595 against cash of 4,875, so the bridge deducts net debt of 6,719 rather than the few hundred previously projected, and the FY2026E year-end path reconciles to it with the December quarter collection as the only step down. Interest is rebuilt at the pack cost of debt on the actual gross debt, annualised from the nine-month charge, with the marginal quarter rate within a tenth of a point of it. Leverage is stated in EBITDA times at the audited year-end so the debt path the rating relies on is visible [S0].

challenges.challenge: The scenario set cannot fail: base 5,071, bear 3,965 and bull 6,757 are all above the 2,450 price, and the bear's 3pp margin shock (about 14.7% realised) is above the 12.8% gross margin the company actually printed in 2026Q2 (pack quarterly: gross profit 2,490 on revenue 19,466). No scenario varies the multiple, although section 5 says a further de-rating, not a worse harvest, is what hurts the holder, and section 4 says the market is rejecting the margin and the terminal growth.
challenges.answer: The bear is built from a witnessed quarter rather than a notional shock: it holds the second quarter realised gross margin, some five points below the nine-month average, so the set can fail, and it does, because the bear target is below the 2,450 price. That is stated in section 5 as the case to hold in mind. The multiple is deliberately not a fifth shock because the de-rating already sits inside the base: both earnings legs apply the peer median, below the multiple the shares trade on, so a further de-rating to the sector current level is roughly half the base valuation and a multiple shock on top would double-count it [S0, S2].

challenges.challenge: The bear raises working-capital intensity by 3pp, to 24.1%, still 4.4pp below the 28.5% the September balance sheet records, and it carries no interest or leverage leg at all, although debt rose from 6,636 in March to 11,595 in September and interest per quarter from 90 to 196. The cash-conversion failure is the downside the quarter actually delivered.
challenges.answer: The bear working-capital shock is raised off the witnessed September level rather than the old cash ratio, and an interest leg is added: cost of debt up a point on the borrowings that already exist after the September re-anchoring, so the cash-conversion failure the quarter actually delivered is priced in the downside. The bull mirrors all four shocks one for one [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says the supply-guidance asymmetry "lands in the bull's margin leg and its absence in the bear's", but both scenarios apply the same 3pp to the same gross_margin input, so the asymmetry is in the prose only. The S11 removal of the Rp11,000 ex-factory reference, accepted in round 3 as a producer-side benefit, is now described as "ambiguous" without new evidence.
challenges.answer: The prose claim that the asymmetry lands in the scenario weights is deleted. The supply guidance and the chick band are now named and not scored: the circular does not say whether the ceiling or the new floor binds on realised prices, no elasticity is published and the segment reports no price per chick, so neither a cost nor a benefit is booked, and the bull is stated to be the operating mirror only. The reader is still given the sizes the sources support, the chick segment nine-month revenue against the broiler and processed-chicken books, so the asymmetry can be sized without being smuggled into the weights [S11, S13, S2].

challenges.challenge: The free nutritious meals programme is sourced (S3) and section 2 says it puts chicken and eggs into institutional menus, but the note carries no institutional volume in the base or the bull, so a policy-backed demand leg is excluded from both by construction. The bull is then only an operating mirror of the bear.
challenges.answer: Stated as a one-way omitted upside, plainly, so the bull is not read as the full bull. The programme has a policy leg but the only procurement volumes in the archive belong to competitors and no source gives CPIN scale, so no institutional volume is carried in the base or the bull and the gap is reported as a gap rather than bounded with an invented range [S3].

challenges.challenge: The P/E leg is 15.30, the average of the peer median 5.27 and an own-history mean of 25.33 that is four annual observations (31.6, 35.5, 21.0, 13.1) described in the packet as a five-year average. The series is collapsing, the latest print is 13.1x, 14% below the multiple applied, and the EV/EBITDA leg's 10.72 compares with 9.02 at the FY2025 year-end. The mean is price-derived, so it rose from 14.63 to 15.30 as the price rose from 2,370 to 2,450.
challenges.answer: The own-history lookback is disclosed as unusable rather than used: four annual observations spanning a re-rating and a de-rating, whose mean is computed from the price it would then be used to value, which would smuggle a re-rating into a cross-check. The legs stay on the peer median, and because that median is below the market own multiple both legs come out below the price, so the target is half discounted cash flow and half a trough floor rather than a re-rating bet. The industry default blends the two sources and the departure is justified in the valuation paragraph and in the extreme-call justification [S0].

challenges.challenge: The three legs sit on different accounting bases: the DCF uses the restated D&A, while the EV/EBITDA leg applies 10.72x to FY2025A EBITDA of 8,443.6 that the note itself calls understated; on the restated basis (9,420) the same multiple gives about Rp5,750, not 5,108. Separately, COE of 13.2% is above the house 11-13% band and is justified only by a balance-of-payments sentence with no source, while WACC of 11.9% uses a 22.4% debt weight against 14% net debt to market.
challenges.answer: Each divergence is explained rather than averaged away. The P/E leg matches the DCF basis; the EV/EBITDA leg still applies the peer multiple to the pack understated EBITDA and is disclosed as the one leg on the bad basis, so it reads as a floor. The cost of equity lands a fifth of a point above the house band on the macro deck inputs and is disclosed rather than massaged through the beta or an override, while the WACC itself is inside the band. The debt weight uses gross borrowings at the valuation date, not net debt, and the two-fifths-of-a-point difference netting would make is stated [S0].

challenges.challenge: The DCF is struck at 30 September 2026 (FY2026E fraction 0.2519, time 0) and then rolled a full year at 13.21% to Rp5,071, so the target is dated about 30 September 2027, 10.5 months from the 13 November price. The 122.4% expected return is therefore a 13.5-month figure and the roll adds about 1.6% the horizon does not support.
challenges.answer: A target-date paragraph is added: the target is dated twelve months from the 30 September valuation anchor, so roughly 30 September 2027 and just over ten months from the 13 November price, and the roll is stated as running long for that horizon rather than silently corrected in the arithmetic [S0].

challenges.challenge: The extreme_call BLOCK justification still cites the prior model: DCF Rp4,382, price Rp2,370, P/E Rp5,035 and EV/EBITDA Rp5,058, against this model's 4,168, 2,450, 5,265 and 5,108. Section 4 says the price is "roughly half" of the DCF when 2,450 over 4,168 is 58.8%, and section 3 says the pack's IDR310bn charge implies a forty-four-year life when 18,060 over 310.5 is 58 years (44 is right only for the 411 default).
challenges.answer: The extreme-call justification is regenerated against the corrected model rather than inherited: the base rests on the nine-month actuals, on cost of goods sold growing more slowly than sales in the witnessed period, and on the EBITDA basis correction, and it notes that the price-implied forward multiple sits above the peer legs, which is why half the target is written down to a trough floor. The fifty-eight-year life implied by the pack depreciation field against its own property, plant and equipment is stated in section 3 with the three anchors that bracket the real charge, so the restatement is visibly a derivation and not a read [S0, S2, S6].

challenges.challenge: The gross_margin input of 19.95% is described as "the margin at last year's input cost", but FY2025A realised 17.6% at those costs, so the input is a 2.3pp calibration residual. The consequence is that the 2pp sensitivity and the FY2027E onward fade are measured off a level no year has earned, and if corn reverted to the FY2025A level the model would print a 19.95% margin.
challenges.answer: gross_margin is labelled for what it is: a calibrated residual set at the FY2025A input cost, not a rate any year earned on its reported basis, because the engine charges the deck corn and soymeal curves on top of it. The report says the two together reproduce the witnessed realised margin and the sensitivity table is read in realised terms, so no reader mistakes the input for an observed rate [S0, S2].

challenges.challenge: Q10 is unfixed. Section 4 prints 'CPIN at 7.1x trailing sits above the median of 5.3 times', but 7.118x is the engine's FY2025A multiple while the 5.27x peer median the legs apply is an LTM figure, so the sentence compares two different bases in the paragraph that just moved the legs onto LTM. On the legs' own basis CPIN trades at 5.4x - at the median, not above it - so the note tells a reader the shares sit at a premium to a sector they are level with. Section 5 then builds on it: 'a further de-rating to the sector's current level is not a scenario - it is roughly half the base valuation'. The base multiple already IS the peer median, so there is no further de-rating left to cost, and a sector-multiple valuation gives Rp2,322-2,398, 62-64% of the Rp3,737 base, not half. Section 4's own adjacent sentence (on trailing earnings the shares are worth about what they cost) is the correct statement.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now labels 7.118x as the FY2025A multiple and states that on the last-twelve-month basis both legs use the shares trade AT the 5.27x peer median, not above it; section 5's de-rating sentence is rebuilt to the arithmetic — base multiple already the peer median, so no further de-rating exists, and a sector-multiple valuation gives the P/E leg about three-fifths of the base, not half.

challenges.challenge: The target has moved from Rp5,240 (published 2026-11-12) to Rp3,945, a 25% cut, and the note never states the prior target or reconciles the legs. The body's investment summary attributes the change to the earnings basis - 'both cross-checks now run on the last twelve months' - but moving FY2025A to LTM earnings on higher LTM profit RAISES the multiple legs; the driver of the cut is the multiple LEVEL, own-history mean to peer median (P/E 5.27x gives Rp2,398 and EV/EBITDA 4.88x gives Rp2,665), while the DCF rose to Rp4,505. As printed, the body explains its largest change with the one input that pushed the other way, and only the front-matter summary and section 4 name the real driver.
challenges.answer: New paragraph 'The target move reconciled' in section 4 states the prior published target of Rp5,240 (12 November), the prior own-history mean multiples and earlier DCF, and walks DCF, P/E, EV/EBITDA, blend, twelve-month roll and scenario weighting to the current Rp3,945; the investment summary now attributes the quarter cut to the multiple level (own-history mean to peer median), with the earnings basis and the higher DCF said to have pushed value up, matching the front-matter summary.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 pairs the probabilities with the values in the wrong order: '50.0% base, 25.0% bear and 25.0% bull, valuing the shares at Rp2,186, Rp3,737 and Rp6,121'. Read positionally the 50% base carries Rp2,186, 11% below the Rp2,450 price, in a note rated BUY at Rp3,945 with a 70.4% return. The values are right and the following sentence identifies the bear correctly, but the published pairing states the opposite of the call (QC Q11, unfixed).
challenges.answer: Both places the scenario set is printed now pair each probability with its own value: in section 4 and section 5, 50% base at Rp3,737, 25% bear at Rp2,186 and 25% bull at Rp6,121, so the positional misread is gone.

missing_bull_case.note: The removal of the Rp11,000 ex-factory DOC reference, which round 3 accepted as a producer-side benefit, is now called "ambiguous" with no new evidence. The supply-cut asymmetry the note itself argues (book about 10x the segment it costs) sits in neither scenario because bull and bear are both a 3pp mirror. Free-meals volume is zero in base and bull.

missing_bear_case.note: No scenario is below the Rp2,450 price and none carries the de-rating the note names as the real risk. The bear's realised gross margin (about 14.7%) is above the 12.8% the company printed in 2026Q2, and the 9M cash-flow collapse (LTM OCF 1,873 against NP 7,461) and the debt build are absent from it.

assumption_realism.note: nwc_pct is held at 21.07% while the 30 September balance sheet shows 28.5% of LTM revenue; FY2026E delta NWC of 1,618 against +6,756 in the nine months; FY2026E net debt of 294 against 6,719 at 30 September; and the opex ratio carries the pack's D&A while D&A is restated up 4x.

evidence_and_citations.note: S2, S11, S13 and S5 quotes check out and no broker material is used (S4 carries a Phintraco target and is correctly uncited). But the extreme_call justification still cites the prior model (DCF 4,382, price 2,370, PE 5,035, EV/EBITDA 5,058), and "roughly half" is 58.8%.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF primary is right for the industry and the 30 September bridge date is consistent. But the multiple legs average a peer median with a 4-observation own-history mean of a collapsing series described as "five-year"; the EV/EBITDA leg uses un-restated EBITDA while the DCF uses restated; COE 13.2% is outside the 11-13% band on an unsourced argument; and the roll prices a 13.5-month horizon.

flags.message: expected return +70%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers produce the return, and the target is deliberately not the cash-flow value. First, the nine-month 2026 result is an actual: net sales of IDR60,200bn against IDR50,600bn and attributable profit of IDR5,180bn (S2, F1, F2, F12). Second, the margin is sourced arithmetic, not a forecast: cost of goods sold grew 16.7 per cent against sales growth of 19.0 per cent (S2, F1, F2, F10), and the deck corn and soymeal curves are charged from FY2026E, so no give-back is assumed. Third, the EBITDA basis is corrected: the pack depreciation line is a fifty-eight-year artefact and its cash flow carries the unnamed add-back, so the forecast charges depreciation within the pack own total operating expense (S0). What the price implies is stated in section 4 and it is not comfortable for the call: at the price the shares capitalise FY2026E earnings at the multiple shown, and the two earnings cross-checks, struck on the witnessed last twelve months because the peer medians they apply are trailing multiples, land at the price rather than far below it - the P/E leg at 2,398 and the EV/EBITDA leg at 2,665 against a 2,450 price (S0, S2). So the market is priced for a trough on trailing earnings and the whole of the return above the price is the cash flow the DCF capitalises, not a re-rating of the multiple; the DCF does embed a terminal exit multiple above today's entry, which section 4 states rather than hides, and that is why half the weight is written down to the peer median. FY2027E revenue growth of 7.0 per cent against the 19.0 per cent FY2026E is a judgment, not a disclosed plan: the FY2026E rate is the nine-month actual for a price-led recovery and no source discloses capacity or a price schedule that repeats it, so the base carries volume plus a modest price and is flagged here rather than buried (S0, S2). The reverse DCF cannot bracket the price - growth alone cannot be pushed low enough - so the reading is stated directly rather than computed (S0).
